parameters.query:
-- Step 4: Atomic insert = idempotency (DEV tables: support_dev).
-- If this update_id already exists, ON CONFLICT skips the insert (no error, no duplicate row).
-- "inserted" tells the next node whether this execution is the first one to see this message.
WITH ins AS (
  INSERT INTO support_dev.messages (update_id, chat_id, text)
  VALUES ($1::bigint, $2::bigint, $3::text)
  ON CONFLICT (update_id) DO NOTHING
  RETURNING update_id
)
SELECT
  $1::bigint AS update_id,
  EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM ins) AS inserted;

-- Step 6: last 5 question/answer pairs BEFORE the current message (DEV tables: support_dev).
-- "update_id < current" = a message sent after this one (processed in parallel) never leaks into its context,
--   and the current message is not repeated.
-- Failed messages are skipped. A 'received' message is included only if it is recent
--   (it is being answered right now); older ones are stuck and would only confuse the AI.
SELECT COALESCE(json_agg(h ORDER BY h.update_id), '[]'::json) AS history
FROM (
  SELECT update_id, text, response_text, status
  FROM support_dev.messages
  WHERE chat_id = $1::bigint
    AND update_id < $2::bigint
    AND (status = 'processed' OR (status = 'received' AND created_at > now() - interval '5 minutes'))
  ORDER BY update_id DESC
  LIMIT 5
) h;

nodes.name: Get Context
nodes.notes: Step 6: last 5 question/answer pairs BEFORE this message. Always returns 1 row.

nodes.name: Build Prompt
nodes.notes: Turns the history + current message into the prompt for the AI Agent.

nodes.name: Prepare Reply
nodes.notes: Empty reply → error. Long reply → cut under Telegram's 4096 limit. Escapes HTML.

parameters.query:
-- Step 8: the answer was delivered -> mark processed and save it (DEV tables: support_dev).
-- response_text is what makes the next messages' context a real Q/A history.
-- tool_calls records which tools the AI used: [] = none.
UPDATE support_dev.messages
SET status = 'processed',
    response_text = $2::text,
    tool_calls = $3::jsonb,
    route = $4::varchar
WHERE update_id = $1::bigint
RETURNING update_id, status, route, jsonb_array_length(tool_calls) AS tool_call_count;

nodes.name: Mark Processed
nodes.notes: Step 8: status = processed + save the answer (it becomes context for the next messages).

nodes.name: General Reply
nodes.notes: Greetings / thanks: fixed reply, no LLM.

nodes.name: Unclear Reply
nodes.notes: Topic not clear (also the classifier's 'other' fallback): ask to clarify, no LLM.

nodes.name: Error Reply
nodes.notes: Router failed (429 / down / bad JSON): fixed apology instead of silence.

parameters.query:
-- Is this Telegram chat linked to an active employee?
-- DEMO: a new chat gets its OWN demo employee (a copy of NXR-1001 with the same balances and attendance),
-- so every visitor can try every feature right away, and one visitor's requests never show up for another.
WITH linked AS (
  SELECT employee_code, full_name_ar, gender FROM hr.employees
  WHERE telegram_chat_id = $1::bigint AND employment_status = 'active'
), new_emp AS (
  INSERT INTO hr.employees (employee_code, full_name_ar, full_name_en, gender, birth_date, hire_date, job_title_ar,
                            department_code, manager_code, employment_status, work_email, telegram_chat_id)
  SELECT 'DEMO-' || $1::text, full_name_ar, full_name_en, gender, birth_date, hire_date, job_title_ar,
         department_code, manager_code, 'active', 'demo+' || $1::text || '@nexora.example', $1::bigint
  FROM hr.employees WHERE employee_code = 'NXR-1001' AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM linked)
  RETURNING employee_code, full_name_ar, gender
), new_bal AS (
  INSERT INTO hr.leave_balances (employee_code, balance_year, leave_type, entitled_days, carried_days)
  SELECT n.employee_code, b.balance_year, b.leave_type, b.entitled_days, b.carried_days
  FROM new_emp n, hr.leave_balances b WHERE b.employee_code = 'NXR-1001'
  RETURNING 1
), new_att AS (
  INSERT INTO hr.attendance (employee_code, work_date, day_status, check_in, check_out, late_minutes)
  SELECT n.employee_code, a.work_date, a.day_status, a.check_in, a.check_out, a.late_minutes
  FROM new_emp n, hr.attendance a WHERE a.employee_code = 'NXR-1001'
  RETURNING 1
)
SELECT COALESCE(
  (SELECT json_build_object('linked', true, 'employee_code', employee_code, 'name', full_name_ar, 'gender', gender) FROM linked),
  (SELECT json_build_object('linked', true, 'demo', true, 'employee_code', employee_code, 'name', full_name_ar, 'gender', gender) FROM new_emp),
  json_build_object('linked', false)) AS me,
  (SELECT count(*) FROM new_bal) + (SELECT count(*) FROM new_att) AS demo_rows_seeded;

nodes.name: Check Link
nodes.notes: Every message: linked employee -> normal flow; not linked -> onboarding (code + birth date).

-- One row per answered message: the router dataset (DEV tables: support_dev).
INSERT INTO support_dev.router_decisions
  (update_id, execution_id, chat_id, request_text, history_count, route, decided_by, router_model, router_error, faq_hit, faq_top_score)
VALUES ($1::bigint, $2::text, $3::bigint, $4::text, $5::int, $6::text, $7::text, NULLIF($8::text, ''), NULLIF($9::text, ''), NULLIF($10::text, '')::boolean, NULLIF($11::text, '')::numeric)
ON CONFLICT (update_id) DO NOTHING;
